Unused Campus Center Meal Swipes do not roll over week to week. They reset every Sunday.
Trojan Plan ($4,840/semester)
For added flexibility and variety, the Trojan Plan is a declining balance plan that is 100% composed of Dining Dollars. Dining Dollars may be used at any Residential Dining Hall or on-campus retail cafe. This plan is an optional upgrade.
Plan features:
$4,840 worth of Dining Dollars per semester
Flex120 Plan ($2,074/semester)

Flex120 Plan ($2,074/semester)
All sophomores, juniors, and seniors living in USC Housing Apartments will be assigned the Flex120 plan when they confirm a USC Housing contract. This plan includes 120 meal swipes that can be used at all three Residential Dining Halls or at most Ronald Tutor Campus Center food court locations and Trojan Grounds, plus $150 Dining Dollars per semester. Residents may elect to upgrade their meal plan.
If you exhaust your Flex120 plan and decide that you want a new plan, you can purchase a new Flex120, Community 25, or Community 50 plan when the Meal Swipes run out. Any unused Dining Dollar or swipe balance will reset (forfeited) at the end of the semester.
Graduate students are not required to purchase a meal plan, but are welcome to do so.

120 Meal Swipes that may be used at all three Residential Dining Halls or at most Ronald Tutor Campus Center food court locations and Trojan Grounds

chunks.title: Contact Us - USC Transportation
chunks.text:
Having trouble finding our office? We are located at 620 West McCarthy Way, (the McCarthy Parking Structure) on the University Park Campus. The arrow on the map below points directly to our front door. If you are driving, enter through the McCarthy Way entrance located at Figueroa and McCarthy Way as shown.
Daily parking is available in McCarthy Way Structure and can be purchased using our Text2Park technology or the pay station located in the Northwest Corner of the structure. Parking rates are $20/day plus a one-time fee of $0.50. For more information please contact Customer Service directly at 213-740-3575. We’ll see you soon!
Our office at the University Park Campus is open from 8:30AM to 3:00PM Monday through Friday. Our UPC office will continue to assist with immobilization requests only, from 3:00PM to 5:00PM. Our office at the Health Sciences Campus is open from 7:30AM to 4:00PM Monday through Friday. Both offices are closed weekends and University Holidays.
AFTER HOURS ASSISTANCE:
If you need assistance with a vehicle boot release or facility access after 5:00pm, please contact the USC Department of Public Safety: (Non-Emergency: 213-740-6000; Emergency: 213-740-4321)

chunks.title: About USC Buses - USC Transportation
chunks.text:
USC Transportation provides an extensive network of free buses throughout the year for students, staff, faculty, university guests, and the local community. Multiple routes service USC’s main campus, the North University Park neighborhood, the USC Parking Center as well as the USC Health Sciences Campus, Marina Del Rey ISI/ICT locations, and even Union Station.
Whether you are commuting to work, getting around campus between classes, or just exploring the wider Los Angeles community our bus system makes it easy. Keep up to date with schedules or even track a bus while you wait!
Latest USC Transportation Announcements

chunks.title: Daily and Hourly Parking - USC Transportation
chunks.text:
Visiting USC for the day or just a few hours? Guests can now purchase short-term or all-day parking using their credit card, using either Text2Park (T2P) on their mobile device or by entering their vehicle license plate in a nearby Pay-By-Plate (PBP) station.
PLEASE NOTE: You may never use spaces marked as “RESERVED” – please park in any normal, unreserved space in the T2P area, or in specifically-marked Pay-By-Plate areas. Sales at any location may close due to limited space availability. Rates may differ on special event/USC home football game days.
See the matrix below for USC T2P / PBP areas, rates, codes, etc. NOTE: During the summer semester ONLY, Downey Structure is available for all-day sales. See the matrix for Fall/Spring hours.

chunks.title: Bus Schedules - USC Transportation
chunks.text:
Fall Semester 2026 Route Schedule – begins Monday, August 24, 2026
Hello Trojans! Our 2026 Fall Semester bus routes begin Monday, August 24, 2026.
Here are the changes that will take effect:
The Marina Del Rey service will only have 5 trips per day, departing USC at 8:05am, 10:00am, 12:00pm, 3:40pm, and 5:45pm.
The C-Route will begin at 6:30am.
The Parking Center Route will run from 9am-3pm.
The Busway Route is replaced with the Circuit Tram.
The Circuit Tram will depart every 30 minutes from 7am-8:30am.
The Circuit Tram route will run every 20 minutes from 9am-4:40pm.
The Soto Route will run from 6:40am to 6:00pm.
Some Union Station service times have been adjusted:
The first Union Station to HSC shuttle is now at 6:35am.
The first Union Station to UPC shuttle is now 6:33am.
New GPS Tracking System and Mobile App

chunks.title: Parking Violations - USC Transportation
chunks.text:
Below are listed some of the common violations we encounter, and a short description/fine for each. For more information regarding a specific violation, please check our Parking Rules and Regulations page, or contact our Enforcement team directly via email at parkingcitations@usc.edu.
Parking Violations
Violation
Minimum Fine
NON-DESIGNATED PARKING AREA
All vehicles are required to park within properly marked designated parking spaces. Vehicles parked in areas other than those designated for parking will be in violation and may be subject to citation.
$65
BLOCKING DRIVEWAY
No vehicle shall block any driveway within the property at any time. Blocking or preventing entry or exiting of vehicles into any area is a violation.
$65
PARKED IN/ON SIDEWALK
No person shall park a vehicle in or on a sidewalk at anytime. A vehicle left (attended or unattended) that causes pedestrian thoroughfare to go around the vehicle is in violation. This type of violation creates a safety hazard.
$65
DOUBLE PARKED
No vehicle may park in any way that inhibits the ability of an adjacent vehicle to access their own space. Vehicles parked in this manner may be subject to citation.
$65
PARKED THE WRONG WAY

chunks.title: Parking Violations - USC Transportation
chunks.text:
bits the ability of an adjacent vehicle to access their own space. Vehicles parked in this manner may be subject to citation.
$65
PARKED THE WRONG WAY
No vehicle shall park on the side of the street facing oncoming traffic at anytime. Vehicles parked in this manner will be in violation.
$65
INCORRECT PARKING AREA
No vehicle shall park in an area for which their issued permit is not valid. For additional information about where and when specific permits are valid, please Consult the "Where Can I Park?" document located online here.
$65
NO VALID PERMIT DISPLAYED
All vehicles are required to have a valid USC PARKING PERMIT/ DAILY PASS AT ALL TIMES. All USC parking permits and daily passes must be displayed in accordance with our Rules and Regulations at all times when the vehicle is parked within the property. Failure to display a valid USC parking permit/daily pass properly, EVEN IF THE PERMIT OR PASS IS VALID, creates this violation.
$65
IMPROPER PERMIT DISPLAY

chunks.title: Parking Violations - USC Transportation
chunks.text:
re to display a valid USC parking permit/daily pass properly, EVEN IF THE PERMIT OR PASS IS VALID, creates this violation.
$65
IMPROPER PERMIT DISPLAY
All USC parking permits/daily passes shall be displayed in one of two ways: Window Sticker permits/daily passes must be displayed right-side up, on the lower left-hand (driver's side) corner of the windshield. Permits must be affixed to the windshield solely by the adhesive on the permit; no tape or any additional adhesive is allowed. No plastic can be attached to this window sticker. Daily Passes must be placed on the lower left-hand corner of the windshield with the daily pass information clearly visible. Failure to display a USC permit/daily pass properly as required will be in violation.
$25
PERMIT NOT REGISTERED TO VEHICLE
All vehicles displaying a USC parking permit MUST be listed in the owner's account with USC Transportation. This includes any secondary vehicle. Any vehicle parked on the property displaying a valid USC permit, but is not registered with our office is in violation and may be cited.
$25
RESERVED PARKING

chunks.title: Parking Violations - USC Transportation
chunks.text:
cle parked on the property displaying a valid USC permit, but is not registered with our office is in violation and may be cited.
$25
RESERVED PARKING
No student, faculty, staff, guest or vendors shall park in any reserved/assigned spaces at any time unless you are the owner of that space and have the required permit properly displayed. Those vehicles parked in such spaces without displaying the proper permit will be in violation and subject to citation, immobilization and/or tow. Residents are required to park only in those spaces/areas assigned to their residence. Vehicles parked in a reserved parking space other than assigned by the Property Manager will be in violation.
$80
RESTRICTED PARKING
No vehicle shall park in any area/space designated as Restricted. Restricted areas have required signage that dictates what type of valid USC permits/daily passes are allowed. Please read signage at the entrance to all lots and open areas on the property prior to parking. Failure to read the posted signs or adhere to its listed restrictions will be in violation of the parking rules/regulations.
$65
PAY-BY-PLATE AREA or TEXT2PARK VIOLATION

chunks.title: Parking Violations - USC Transportation
chunks.text:
posted signs or adhere to its listed restrictions will be in violation of the parking rules/regulations.
$65
PAY-BY-PLATE AREA or TEXT2PARK VIOLATION
ALL USC Pay-by-Plate areas and Text2Park zones are enforced 24 hours a day. USC permits or daily passes are NOT allowed to park in designated Pay-by-Plate areas. Failure to pay for time spent in Pay-by-Plate or Text2Park areas is in violation of our parking rules/regulations.
$65
*see EVENT EXCEPTION below
PAY-BY-PLATE AREA or TEXT2PARK VIOLATION - EVENT EXCEPTION
Same rules/regulations as the entry above this one, but an increased fine is levied during USC home football games and other campus-wide special events (athletic events, concerts, festivals, etc.)
$80
TIME ZONE VIOLATION
No vehicle shall park in a designated space/area beyond the posted time zone restrictions. Those vehicles exceeding the time restrictions will be in violation.
$65
LOADING/UNLOADING YELLOW ZONE VIOLATION

chunks.title: Parking Violations - USC Transportation
chunks.text:
nd the posted time zone restrictions. Those vehicles exceeding the time restrictions will be in violation.
$65
LOADING/UNLOADING YELLOW ZONE VIOLATION
Vehicles parked for the purpose of loading/unloading of persons and/or materials must use designated yellow zones only. Any other area used for this purpose is in violation. Vehicles using this Yellow Zone must display a special permit/pass that can only be issued from a Campus Gate Attendant or USC Transportation office. Any vehicle parked not displaying this special pass is in violation. Vehicles using this Yellow Zone displaying the required pass are parked in a time limit zone. Please adhere to the posted time limit. Any vehicle staying longer than the posted allowed time is in violation.
$65
POSTED NO PARKING/RED ZONE
RED ZONE
No vehicle may park in any area where a curb is painted RED for any period of time. Vehicles parked in these zones will be in violation.
NO PARKING ZONE
No vehicle may park in any area identified and/or posted as a NO PARKING ZONE for any period of time. Vehicles parked in these zones will be in violation.
$100
FIRE LANE

chunks.title: Parking Violations - USC Transportation
chunks.text:
in any area identified and/or posted as a NO PARKING ZONE for any period of time. Vehicles parked in these zones will be in violation.
$100
FIRE LANE
No vehicle may park in any area identified and/or posted as a FIRE LANE for any period of time. Vehicles parked in these areas will be in violation and are subject to citation and/or tow.
$100
PARKING WITHIN 15FT OF FIRE HYDRANT
No vehicle shall park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant on either side. Curbs or sidewalks do not have to be colored where a fire hydrant is located. Vehicles parked in these areas will be in violation and are subject to citation and/or tow.
$100
WHEELCHAIR ACCESS-SIDEWALK/RAMP
No person shall stop, park, or leave standing any vehicle, whether attended or unattended, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a peace officer or official traffic control device, in front of that portion of a curb that has been cut down, lowered, or constructed to provide wheelchair accessibility to the sidewalk and that is designated for wheelchair access by either a sign or red paint on the curb.
$200
DISABLED PARKING/NO PLACARD DISPLAYED

chunks.title: Parking Violations - USC Transportation
chunks.text:
ity to the sidewalk and that is designated for wheelchair access by either a sign or red paint on the curb.
$200
DISABLED PARKING/NO PLACARD DISPLAYED
No person shall stop, park, or leave standing any vehicle, whether attended or unattended, in a stall or space designated for disabled persons and disabled veterans, unless the vehicle displays either a special identification license plate or a distinguishing placard issued by a state DMV office (in addition to a USC parking permit or daily pass).
$300
OBSTRUCT/BLOCK DISABLED BLUE ZONE
No person shall stop, park, or leave standing any vehicle, whether attended or unattended, in a manner that would obstruct, block, or otherwise bar access to those parking areas or spaces indicated as being reserved for use by handicapped individuals.
$200
DISABLED (CROSSHATCH) LOAD/UNLOAD
No person shall stop, park, or leave standing any vehicle, whether attended or unattended, including a vehicle displaying a special identification license plate or a distinguishing placard issued by a state DMV office, in either of the following places:

chunks.title: Parking Violations - USC Transportation
chunks.text:
vehicle displaying a special identification license plate or a distinguishing placard issued by a state DMV office, in either of the following places:
- On the lines marking the boundaries of a parking stall or space designated for disabled persons or disabled veterans.
- In any area of the pavement adjacent to a parking stall or space designated for disabled persons or disabled veterans that is marked by crosshatched lines and is thereby designated for the loading and unloading of vehicles parked in the adjacent stall or space.
$200
IMMOBILIZATION
Vehicles may be immobilized for having outstanding administrative fees from various violation(s) previously issued, if the vehicle is displaying a permit previously reported lost, missing or stolen, or is displaying a permit that has been forged or altered. All related or outstanding fees (plus a Boot release fee) must be paid before a Boot can be released.
$100
IMMOBILIZATION DEVICE DAMAGE
Damaging/removing the impound parking device plus any replacement cost associated for its repair or replacement deemed by USC Transportation.
$200
ALTERED PERMIT OR PASS

chunks.title: Parking Violations - USC Transportation
chunks.text:
he impound parking device plus any replacement cost associated for its repair or replacement deemed by USC Transportation.
$200
ALTERED PERMIT OR PASS
Any vehicle displaying a USC parking permit or pass that has been altered IN ANY WAY is subject to immobilization and all related fees, which may include corresponding "usage" fees (e.g., if a semesterly permit is altered, the violator will also be charged for a semesterly permit, in addition to all other fees).
$500
FORGED PERMIT OR PASS
Any vehicle displaying a USC parking permit or pass that is a forgery (i.e., via photocopy, photograph, computer editing software, etc.) is subject to immobilization and related fees which may include "usage" fees (e.g., if a semesterly permit is forged, the violator will also be charged for a semesterly permit, in addition to all other fees).
$999
RESTRICTED PARKING - UNIVERSITY VILLAGE GARAGE
No vehicle may park in the University Village garage without paying an hourly rate for (or having validated completely or in part) the right to do so.
$80
ZIPCAR RESERVED SPACE

chunks.title: Parking Violations - USC Transportation
chunks.text:
University Village garage without paying an hourly rate for (or having validated completely or in part) the right to do so.
$80
ZIPCAR RESERVED SPACE
No student, faculty, staff, guest or vendors shall park in any marked Zipcar Car Sharing reserved/assigned spaces at any time unless you are the renter/driver of the Zipcar vehicle assigned to that space. Those vehicles parked in such spaces will be in violation and subject to citation, immobilization and/or tow.
$80

chunks.text:
On-Campus Jobs
USC hires student workers year-round across a wide range of campus departments. Opportunities are available in research labs, academic and administrative offices, libraries, and campus partners like the USC Bookstore. These roles allow students to gain valuable experience, build transferable skills, and earn income while staying connected to campus.
How do I find on-campus jobs?
Students can find both work-study and non-work-study on-campus jobs through Handshake. To search for these positions:
Log in to Handshake
Select “Jobs”
Click on “All filters”
Check the “On Campus Student Employment” option under “Job Type”
Most on-campus job openings for the fall semester are posted by the first or second week of August. However, departments continue to post opportunities throughout the year based on hiring needs.
Campus Departments That Hire Students
Additionally, there are a number of on-campus departments that have application information on their websites. Review Find On-Campus Student Jobs for more information.

Not sure if you have work-study?
Learn more about work-study eligibility
Please note: International students are not eligible for work-study positions. For information about on-campus employment for F-1 international students, visit the Office of International Services (OIS) website.

Find meaningful ways to give back while developing transferable skills such as teamwork, leadership, and civic engagement.

Internship Guide
The USC Career Center’s Internship Engagement Office is designed to help explore the many resources, programs, and collaborative opportunities available to support your career journey. We encourage you to learn about the internship process, engage in career programming, and connect with resources across the USC community.
For a video overview, please review the following recordings from our Internships 101: Finding & Applying For Internships:
Handshake: Getting Ready for Fall Recruitment
Undergraduate Students
Graduate Students
International Students
We encourage students to seek internships for the following benefits:
Apply your strengths, coursework and group experiences into real world applications
Gain training and connections in a particular field, industry, and organization
Enhance your professional experience and identify mentors in your areas of expertise
Access potential pipeline for future roles and full-time employment post-graduation
To get started, consider:
Exploring options
Making connections (with the industry/field/job function/geographic location)
Balancing an Internship (part-time/full-time internships during the fall/spring/summer)

chunks.title: Internship Guide – Career Center | University of Southern California
chunks.text:
ons (with the industry/field/job function/geographic location)
Balancing an Internship (part-time/full-time internships during the fall/spring/summer)
Explore Options
Most organizations are looking for candidates to fill an immediate opening. This typically means you should be applying the semester prior to the anticipated start date. Similarly, most internship recruitment occurs at least a semester (sometimes a year) in advance. However, depending on the industry/organization you are targeting, you may have to apply earlier. Refer to the guide below for a general timeline. (Note: This may not apply to every organization, so please do your research!)
Search by career topic, industry or student community to discover online resources and opportunities in Handshake that support your goals.
Make Connections
The process for securing an internship takes time and can involve many steps. We suggest participating in events and speaking with:
Peers: Attend a coffee chat or workshop with an Peer Career Navigator

chunks.title: Internship Guide – Career Center | University of Southern California
chunks.text:
nd can involve many steps. We suggest participating in events and speaking with:
Peers: Attend a coffee chat or workshop with an Peer Career Navigator
Staff: Join the Networking Hub (smaller group sessions) to learn how to start the process, learn about expectations and how to maintain these critical events. Join us for an Industry Trek to meet the employees in the industry you’re interested in.
Faculty: Take advantage of office hours to speak with your professors about their academic/industry expertise.
USC Alums: Request for informational interviews (informal coffee chats) to gain more insight into their career launch and professional experiences as you pave the way for your chosen path through the Trojan Network and LinkedIn.
Need a headshot or looking to gain an overview of LinkedIn to start this process? Check out our Headshots to Handshakes program.
Balancing an Internship
Internships are offered each semester (fall/spring/summer) for at least 6 weeks/term. Most students choose to work between 8 – 20 hours to balance coursework and other obligations. During the summer, many students opt to intern full-time (40 hours/week) when not enrolled in classes.

chunks.text:
rs to balance coursework and other obligations. During the summer, many students opt to intern full-time (40 hours/week) when not enrolled in classes.
Course Credit If an employer requires course credit (speak with the HR department or supervisor for clarification), USC offers several courses for internships year round and MDA 250 is open to all students, in all majors. You must already have secured an internship to obtain D-clearance.

Job Search Guide
The following guide is a compilation of strategies and resources available to you to help guide your job search.
Get Started:
Reflect on your skills, interests, and values. For an overview refer to the Career Exploration.
Narrow down your job search parameters (desired industry, job function, geographic location)
Consider the application timeline (some industries have rolling applications while others have targeted, seasonal hiring)
Identify what employers are looking for:
The National Association of Colleges & Employers (NACE) annually compiles a list of competencies employers seek on resumes.
The 15 Fastest-Growing Skills in the US (LinkedIn News)
Resumes/Cover Letters
Review some quick tips & sample docs if you need some quick tips & sample resumes/cover letters. Downloadable MS word templates are available on Handshake in the resource library.
Meet with an advisor The Career Center offers drop-in advising (no appointment required) on weekdays from 1pm to 3:30pm in STU-110. Just bring your resume or cover letter (print out or on your device) and check in at the front desk with your student ID number.

chunks.title: Job Search Guide – Career Center | University of Southern California
chunks.text:
to 3:30pm in STU-110. Just bring your resume or cover letter (print out or on your device) and check in at the front desk with your student ID number.
Virtual Self-Guided Resume Reviews & Generative AI review Supplement an advisor review with AI-powered feedback. Upload your resume to Quinncia for instant feedback. You can also check out the “Resume, Cover Letter, and C.V. Resources” in the resources tab on Handshake or view our AI Guidelines page for tips/prompts to help you get started.
Industry Exploration
With your degree you might have the opportunity to work in a variety of environments ranging from the private sector, federal government, nonprofits, and start-ups, but which one is the best fit?
Review Industry Exploration Resources on Handshake and a list of Interests/Industries.
Vault offers industry guides detailing jobs, salary/location info, and more!
Professional Associations are organized groups focused on advancing and connecting individuals within a particular profession. Most offer websites that contain insights on what it’s like to work in the industry and these are great pages to follow on LinkedIn.

chunks.title: Job Search Guide – Career Center | University of Southern California
chunks.text:
cular profession. Most offer websites that contain insights on what it’s like to work in the industry and these are great pages to follow on LinkedIn.
Want to see what industries recent USC graduates found jobs in? Check out Career Outcomes from the Career Center’s First Destination Survey.
In addition to exploring industries it is helpful to identify in demand skills.
Each year NACE (National Association of Colleges & Employers) surveys hiring managers regarding the attributes employers look for on resumes. Read Job Outlook 2026
Networking/Informational Interviewing
Applying for a full time job can be quite competitive so leveraging your network is a vital strategy to stand out!
We suggest speaking with:
Peers: Consider scheduling an appointment with an Industry Insider Intern
Faculty: take advantage of office hours to talk to your professors about their academic/industry expertise

Identifying Job Leads
Students can find jobs promoted at events hosted during On-Campus Recruitment and posted online.
Career Fairs & Other Recruitment Opportunities
Career Fairs We host career fairs during fall and spring semesters. Graduating students still have the opportunity to meet with employers:
Thursday, March 12, 2026 Health and Sciences Virtual Career Fair
Thursday, April 16, 2026 Recent Graduates & Students Virtual Career Fair
Trojan Talks Employers share information about their organizations and provide students a chance to network with recruiters and alumni. To learn more review “What is a Trojan Talk” and view Upcoming Trojan Talks.
Handshake (Online Job Postings & More!)
Handshake is USC’s university-wide career services management platform and the largest career community for college students.

Handshake is USC’s university-wide career services management platform and the largest career community for college students.
In addition to hosting advising appointments and an online career resource library, Handshake serves as a job board and networking tool allowing you to connect with employers hiring for full-time roles.
External Job Boards
We have curated a list of industry-specific job boards for industries including the Arts, Music, Environment/Sustainability, Public Policy, and Management Consulting.
Tip: Visit the page What Can I Do With This Major and select a major/field of interest. Next scroll down to the bottom to view the headings “Related Resources” or “Employment Opportunities” to view additional industry-specific external job boards.

Alternative Options
Temporary to Permanent Roles & Externships
Job shadowing
Forage is a platform providing virtual job simulations and short courses to build real-life skills for real-life roles, offering a window into company and a preview of their day-to-day.
Short term experiences
Parker Dewey provides micro-Internships, short-term, paid, professional projects which are open to all college students and recent graduates of U.S.-based institutions.
Extern provides short, online, project-based work experiences offered by employers ranging from Fortune 500s to startups.
Staffing/Temp Agencies – short term opportunities that might lead to longer term employment
Insight Global

Interviewing & Salary/Offer Negotiation
Interviewing
For an overview visit our Interview Preparation page containing sample questions, tips for navigating different types of interviews, and resources for practice.
The Career Center offers mock interviews upon request and you can also access 24/7 prep using Big Interview (learn more below).
Salary/Offer Negotiation
For an overview visit Salary Negotiation and What To Consider When Evaluating A Job Offer.

Can I still access Handshake & other career resources as an alum?
Handshake
Accessing Handshake Until Graduation: Please be aware that you can continue signing in with your USC NetID and password until you lose access to your USC email which typically occurs within 3-6 months following graduation.
Transition to alumni access without having to sign up again by doing the following:
Update your primary email address to a non-USC email – Step 1 Instructions
Create a new password – Step 2 Instructions
Need Help? If you can’t access Handshake following graduation you may submit the following Alumni Handshake Request Form for assistance.

International Student Information
CPT/OPT & Work Authorization
Curricular Practical Training (CPT) is a type of work authorization that allows F-1 international students to participate in paid off-campus academic internships during their degree program. The purpose of CPT is academic, not just for employment purposes, and the internship must be considered an integral part of a student’s degree program. For more information about CPT please visit the website for the Office of International Students (OIS).
Unpaid Internships
Unpaid internships potentially do not require a formal CPT to be filed. You should review the Department of Labor's (DOL) Fact Sheet #71. This fact sheet provides general information to help determine whether interns and students working for “for-profit” employers are entitled to minimum wages and overtime pay under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA).

chunks.title: Engineering Practicum (Internships) - USC Viterbi | Career Services
chunks.text:
ther interns and students working for “for-profit” employers are entitled to minimum wages and overtime pay under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA).
If the unpaid internship does not satisfy DOL rules regarding volunteer work, then the work is "employment." In this case, an international student can engage in the internship only if he/she/they has proper work authorization. If the student engages in work that does not satisfy DOL rules regarding unpaid internships and does so without proper work authorization, the student is engaging in unauthorized employment and is out of status, even if the student receives no pay.
If you are engaging in bona fide volunteer activity, we advise you to get documentation from the organization explaining the nature of your work. You should keep this with your other immigration records.
If you have further questions we encourage you to schedule an appointment with legal counsel to understand the content of the DOL Fact sheet. The USC Graduate Student Government offers free legal counseling to the USC student population. To make an appointment go to their website: https://gsg.usc.edu/student-resources/

Creating Your Profile: Current Students
Initial Log-In: When you login for the first time, you will be prompted to create your profile and upload a resume into the system. Basic student profile information including your name, major, and school will already be uploaded into your account.
You can select My Profile at any time to add or edit profile information or documents.
The Documents tab will allow you to add resumes, cover letters and other application materials as well as build your profile directly from your uploaded resume.
Special Note: Making your profile and a resume visible to “Community” will allow employers to search for and contact you based on your interests and additional profile information.

Research or Study Abroad
On This Page

How to Conduct Research Abroad as an International Student at USC
Seeking Research Approval
F-1 and J-1 international students who wish to travel abroad to conduct research for their academic program must first consult with and get approval from their academic department. The expected duration of their time abroad should be determined before they depart from the United States.
In addition, graduate students should discuss any possible changes to their university funding (e.g., TA/RAships) with the USC Graduate School, as this could be affected while they are abroad.
Students who will conduct research abroad in their final semester should also consult with OIS about how this could affect their Post-Completion OPT eligibility, as they must be in the United States when they file their OPT application with U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS).
Following Approval
Once a student receives approval from their academic department to conduct research abroad, they must complete the Independent Student Travel Registration Form. If you have questions about this form, email stabroad@usc.edu.

chunks.title: Research or Study Abroad - USC OIS
chunks.text:
t research abroad, they must complete the Independent Student Travel Registration Form. If you have questions about this form, email stabroad@usc.edu.
To comply with immigration regulations, OIS must report scheduled travel related to research abroad to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security via SEVIS each semester. Students who will be out of the country for the majority of or the entire semester for research purposes will receive additional information in the Student Travel Abroad portal, including a link to the OIS Research/Study Abroad Request. Once OIS receives the completed form, the student’s SEVIS record will be updated to reflect approval to conduct research abroad for the upcoming semester. This will support a smooth reentry to the United States. Students who plan to extend their research abroad for more than one semester must enroll in a dissertation or directed research course and submit the Research/Study Abroad Request again.
It is the student’s responsibility to ensure they have valid reentry documents to facilitate their return to the United States.

chunks.title: Pre-Completion OPT | USC OIS
chunks.text:
Pre-Completion OPT
On This Page
Jump to a Section
What Is Pre-Completion OPT?
Pre-Completion Optional Practical Training (OPT) is a type of employment authorization that allows F-1 students to gain practical work experience during their academic program (i.e., before the program end date listed on the Form I-20). It is one of three types of Optional Practical Training available to USC students.
Employment must be directly related to the student’s major field of study at USC. The student is required to maintain F-1 status and report to OIS during the Pre-Completion OPT period.
The Pre-Completion OPT application will require a Form I-20 with the Pre-Completion OPT recommendation on page 3 issued by OIS before filing a formal application using the Form I-765 to USCIS.
Time used for Pre-Completion OPT is deducted from a student’s available 12 months of Post-Completion OPT eligibility after graduation.
Back to Top
Eligibility Requirements for Pre-Completion OPT
To be eligible for Pre-Completion OPT, students:

chunks.title: Pre-Completion OPT | USC OIS
chunks.text:
pletion OPT eligibility after graduation.
Back to Top
Eligibility Requirements for Pre-Completion OPT
To be eligible for Pre-Completion OPT, students:
Must have maintained F-1 status for a minimum of one academic year (i.e., two consecutive academic semesters, not including summer sessions) or will be completing one academic year within 90 days of applying for Pre-Completion OPT.
Must not have accrued 12 months or more of full-time Curricular Practical Training (CPT) at their current degree level. Part-time CPT does not impact OPT eligibility.
Must be in the United States to file Form I-765.
Must only pursue employment directly related to their major field of study.
Must consult with an OIS advisor to determine eligibility.
Are not required to have a job offer.

How to Apply for Pre-Completion OPT
The Pre-Completion OPT application process must be completed in the following order:
Student meets with an OIS advisor to determine eligibility.
Student submits Pre-Completion OPT I-20 Request in Trojan International.
Student receives Pre-Completion OPT I-20 from OIS via USC email.

USCIS adjudicates the student’s Pre-Completion OPT application.
If approved, student receives USCIS approval notification by email and an Employment Authorization Document (EAD) by USPS mail.

When to Submit the Pre-Completion OPT I-20 Request
A student may apply for Pre-Completion OPT up to 90 days before meeting the requirement of one full academic year in F-1 status. However, the requested Pre-Completion OPT start date must be after satisfying the one academic year requirement (i.e., two consecutive academic semesters, not including summer sessions).

OIS recommends submitting the Pre-Completion OPT I-20 Request and filing with USCIS early to avoid delays, as processing times vary significantly.
Selecting a Requested Pre-Completion OPT Start Date
When completing the Pre-Completion OPT I-20 request, students are required to select a preferred start and end date for authorization. OIS suggests selecting a start date that is at least two to three months in the future from the date the application is submitted to USCIS.
Pre-Completion OPT is typically recommended on a semester basis. It cannot extend beyond the Form I-20 program end date. Once the Pre-Completion OPT application is filed with USCIS, the requested start and end dates cannot be changed.
Impact on Post-Completion OPT
All standard Optional Practical Training is capped at a cumulative total of 12 months per degree level. (The 24-month STEM OPT Extension is separate.) Because of this limit, Pre-Completion OPT directly reduces the overall balance, leaving less Post-Completion OPT time after graduation:

Part-Time Deduction: Approved part-time Pre-Completion OPT is subtracted from Post-Completion OPT at a half-time rate. For example, four months of approved part-time Pre-Completion OPT will deduct two months from Post-Completion OPT, with only 10 months of Post-Completion OPT remaining.
Full-Time Deduction: Approved full-time Pre-Completion OPT is subtracted from Post-Completion OPT at a full-time rate. For example, three months of approved full-time Pre-Completion OPT will deduct three months from Post-Completion OPT, with only nine months of Post-Completion OPT remaining.

How to Request a Pre-Completion OPT From OIS
Students can request a Pre-Completion OPT I-20 from OIS through Trojan International.
Students must provide their academic advisor’s contact information so that the advisor can confirm their expected graduation date. This will determine the lastest possible Pre-Completion OPT end date. The advisor listed on the form must be an academic advisor, student support staff member or another designated academic department staff member.
OIS takes 10 business days to process the Pre-Completion OPT I-20 Request. The 10-business-day period does not begin until the student’s academic advisor completes their portion of the Pre-Completion OPT I-20 Request.
An OIS advisor will review the student’s academic and immigration records to determine all Pre-Completion OPT eligibility requirements are met. If a student’s Pre-Completion OPT I-20 Request is incomplete or has errors, OIS will contact the student via their USC email account with instructions on how to correct and resubmit the request form. The 10-business-day processing time will restart once OIS receives the resubmission.

Based on certain classification criteria, the CIP code option that most closely matches the student’s USC program has been designated by the student’s academic department for official use in SEVIS and on the Form I-20. U.S. consular and immigration officers are aware of this, as this happens often, especially with programs that have unique majors/major names.

Students must quickly move on to the next step, filing the Form I-765, as the Pre-Completion OPT I-20 is valid for only 30 days from the I-20 issue date.
Make sure to check the issue date on your Pre-Completion OPT I-20; the Pre-Completion OPT I-20 is valid for only 30 days from that date.

Filing the Form I-765
After receiving the Pre-Completion OPT I-20 from OIS, students must file Form I-765 online via their myUSCIS account. If the student does not have an account with USCIS, they must create one.
Important Deadline Considerations
Students must file the Form I-765 within 30 days of the issue date on page 1 of their Pre-Completion OPT I-20.

Important Deadline Considerations
Students must file the Form I-765 within 30 days of the issue date on page 1 of their Pre-Completion OPT I-20.
If the student misses this 30-day deadline, they must submit the OPT I-20 Reprint (Missed 30 Days/Date Change) Request in Trojan International before submitting the Form I-765 to USCIS.
Students may file the Form I-765 as early as 90 days prior to meeting the one academic year requirement, but must ensure the requested Pre-Completion OPT start date is after they have met this one academic year requirement.
USCIS follows Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) for submission deadlines. Your application must be submitted by 23:59 UTC on the specified deadline, regardless of your local time zone. To avoid denials for missed filing deadlines, we strongly recommend submitting your application at least one day before the due date. Please plan accordingly and confirm UTC conversions for your time zone.
Before You File
Make sure you are physically present in the United States when you file the Form I-765. Filing from outside the United States will result in a denial of your Form I-765.

Ensure your bank account has sufficient funds to cover the non-refundable Form I-765 filing fee to avoid USCIS rejecting your application.
Carefully review our Guide to Filing Form I-765 for Pre-Completion OPT to avoid mistakes that could lead to a rejection, request for evidence or denial of your application. Please note that in order to access this guide, students must log in using their USC email address.
Create a myUSCIS account if needed.
How to File the Form I-765
Students will need to upload a copy of the hand-signed Pre-Completion OPT I-20 along with other supporting documents and pay the non-refundable Form I-765 filing fee with a credit or debit card.
Students who want a response from USCIS before the estimated processing time can apply for Premium Processing for an additional fee.

Students who want a response from USCIS before the estimated processing time can apply for Premium Processing for an additional fee.
To apply for Premium Processing, students can either request it when initially filing the I-765 application or file Form I-907, Request for Premium Processing Service, at a later time. USCIS guarantees a response within 30 business days, not including weekends or holidays, of filing for students who apply for Premium Processing. Attending the required biometrics appointment may reset the processing time. Please refer to the case status section of your myUSCIS portal for additional guidance.
Photo and Biometric Requirements
In December 2025, USCIS updated its policy on how photographs are collected and reused for immigration applications.
At this time, OPT and STEM OPT applicants must still submit two passport-style photos that meet U.S. Department of State passport photograph requirements, in accordance with current USCIS and OIS instructions.

USCIS may also determine that a new photo is needed and may require a biometrics services appointment at a local Application Support Center. If you receive a biometrics notice or scheduling instructions, you must follow them carefully.
Please regularly check your email, USPS mail and USCIS online account for a biometrics notice and to ensure your mailing address is up to date. If you receive any USCIS notice about photos or biometrics and have questions, submit the Request to Review USCIS Notice and then attend OIS advising for assistance.
If you have been notified that a biometrics appointment will be scheduled but have not received your biometrics appointment notice within two weeks, you should submit a USCIS Case Inquiry for Non-Delivery of Notice.

Social Media Vetting
USCIS has expanded the use of social media review in certain immigration applications. As a result, officers will conduct a closer review of a student’s immigration history and compliance with U.S. laws and students’ online activity may be considered as part of USCIS’s vetting process.
Promoting or supporting anti-American or antisemitic views will be considered serious negative factors and may lead to a denial of the application. The new policy is effective Aug. 19, 2025, and applies to both pending requests and those filed on or after that date.

Rejection
If an application is rejected, the student will receive an I-797C Notice of Action: Rejection. USCIS will indicate the reason for rejection on the I-797C. A student who receives a rejection notice should:
Submit the Request to Review USCIS Notice.
Meet with an advisor during OIS drop-in advising to determine eligibility to resubmit Form I-765.
If eligible, request an updated Pre-Completion OPT I-20 using the OPT I-20 Reprint Request in Trojan International.

Request for Evidence
A student may receive a Request for Evidence (RFE) if USCIS needs more information before processing their application, such as if the payment method was not accepted. The RFE will specify which additional documents are required and the specific deadline for responding. The student will need to submit the Request to Review USCIS Notice before responding to the RFE.
Notice of Intent to Deny
Upon review of the supporting evidence, USCIS may identify concerns and issue a Notice of Intent to Deny (NOID). This warning letter allows students to provide any new evidence addressing the concerns noted. The NOID includes a response deadline and failure to respond by that date can result in a denial of their application. The student will need to submit the Request to Review USCIS Notice before responding to the NOID.

Maintaining F-1 Status While on OPT
General Pre-Completion OPT Requirements
In addition to complying with U.S. laws and immigration requirements, failure to meet the following requirements for OPT employment may result in the automatic termination of the student’s SEVIS record by SEVP and/or USCIS.
Direct Relation to Major
Any employment on Pre-Completion OPT must be directly related to the student’s major. USCIS determines whether a job is related. Therefore, the student should be able to:
Provide an explanation to USCIS if asked how their job is related to their major at USC.
On a day-to-day basis, they apply the knowledge they gained from their academic program to their job.
Students will use the following template as a guide if needed in the future: “I work [insert full-time or part-time] as a [insert job title] for [insert employer name]. My duties include [insert list of job duties]. At this job, I use [insert list of relevant skills/knowledge from your coursework], which directly relates to my USC [insert degree level] in [insert field of study].”
Hours of Employment

chunks.title: Pre-Completion OPT | USC OIS
chunks.text:
levant skills/knowledge from your coursework], which directly relates to my USC [insert degree level] in [insert field of study].”
Hours of Employment
The number of hours permitted to work per week depends on whether the student is seeking part-time or full-time authorization:
Part-Time Pre-Completion OPT (20 hours or fewer per week): Students are strictly limited to part-time authorization during the fall and spring semesters.
Full-Time Pre-Completion OPT (More than 20 hours per week): Students may be authorized for full-time work during the official summer vacation period only if continuing their academic program in the subsequent fall semester.
Types of Employment Permitted While on OPT
The following types of employment are permitted while a student is on Pre-Completion OPT:
Standard, part-time or full-time employer: Student works for one employer. Work hours depends on what the Pre-Completion OPT was authorized for.
Multiple employers: Student works for more than one employer.

chunks.title: Pre-Completion OPT | USC OIS
chunks.text:
for one employer. Work hours depends on what the Pre-Completion OPT was authorized for.
Multiple employers: Student works for more than one employer.
Multiple short-term employers: Musicians or other performing artists may work for multiple short-term employers (i.e., gigs). Students should maintain a list of all gigs, including the dates and durations.
Work for hire/contract: Also commonly referred to as “1099 employment,” the term “work for hire” describes a service based on a contractual agreement rather than an employment relationship. This means that the individual is performing a service.
Self-employment: A student may start a business and be self-employed. The student must be able to prove to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security that they have the proper business licenses and are actively engaged in a business related to their degree program. OIS recommends that a self-employed student consult a lawyer.
Employment through an employment/staffing agency or consulting firm: A student may gain employment through a third-party agency.

Employment through an employment/staffing agency or consulting firm: A student may gain employment through a third-party agency.
Unpaid/volunteer jobs: A student may work on a volunteer basis or as an unpaid intern, where this does not violate any U.S. labor laws. Labor laws vary by state. Check with the company’s human resources department for restrictions.

U.S. Address Update
While on Pre-Completion OPT, students must submit the SEVIS U.S. Address and Contact Update via Trojan International within 10 days of any change in their U.S. address. The student must report the following changes:
Adding new employer(s).
Changes to current employment, such as:
Job title
Employer name
Employer worksite address

What Is a STEM OPT Extension?
The STEM OPT Extension is a work authorization for F-1 students who have graduated from an approved STEM field in the United States. As such, students must maintain their F-1 status and continue to report to OIS.
Students currently on Post-Completion OPT can apply for a STEM OPT Extension to extend their current work authorization for an additional 24 months. Employment must be directly related to the student’s STEM degree.
The STEM OPT Extension Application will require a STEM OPT recommendation (STEM OPT Extension I-20) from OIS before filing a formal application (Form I-765) to USCIS.
Back to Top
Eligibility Requirements for a STEM OPT Extension
To be eligible to apply for a STEM OPT Extension, students:
Must currently be in a valid period of Post-Completion OPT.
Must have maintained F-1 status and not accrued more than 90 days of unemployment during their Post-Completion OPT period.
Must work for an employer that meets all of the STEM OPT employment requirements.
Must begin STEM-eligible employment on or before the STEM OPT Extension start date.

chunks.title: STEM OPT Extension - USC OIS
chunks.text:
n employer that meets all of the STEM OPT employment requirements.
Must begin STEM-eligible employment on or before the STEM OPT Extension start date.
Must have submitted the STEM OPT application to USCIS before their Post-Completion EAD end date. USCIS will not approve applications received after the Post-Completion OPT EAD end date. In addition to these filing dates, students must consider other important dates when applying for STEM OPT.
Must be in the United States to file the Form I-765.
Must have completed a bachelor’s, master’s or doctoral STEM-designated degree program at a U.S. institution.* Students can determine whether their degree program is STEM-designated by checking whether the CIP code on page 1 of their Form I-20 appears in the U.S. Department of Homeland Security’s list of STEM-designated programs.
Your degree program’s CIP code can be found under the “Program of Study” section on your Form I-20.

Completing the Form I-983
The “Form I-983 Training Plan for STEM OPT Students” is a document that clearly articulates the student’s learning objectives and affirms the employer’s commitment to helping the student achieve those objectives.
Students can download the Form I-983 from the USCIS website. Students and their employers must complete and sign Form I-983 before students can request their STEM OPT Extension I-20 from OIS.
Refer to our sample Form I-983 for USC graduates for guidance on completing the form correctly. Additional guidance on Form I-983 requirements is available on the Study in the States website. Requesting a STEM OPT Extension I-20
When to Submit the STEM OPT Extension I-20 Request to OIS
The hard deadline for students to request a STEM OPT I-20 from OIS is 15 business days before their Post-Completion OPT EAD end date. However, students may request their STEM OPT I-20 from OIS as early as 90 days before the end date of their Post-Completion OPT EAD.
OIS recommends submitting the STEM OPT I-20 request as soon as the student’s application period opens.
Calculating STEM OPT Extension Start and End Dates

chunks.title: STEM OPT Extension - USC OIS
chunks.text:
recommends submitting the STEM OPT I-20 request as soon as the student’s application period opens.
Calculating STEM OPT Extension Start and End Dates
When completing the STEM OPT Extension I-20 Request, students must enter a STEM OPT Extension start date that is one day after their Post-Completion OPT end date. The system will then automatically calculate the STEM OPT Extension end date to reflect the 24-month extension.
For example, if a student’s post-completion OPT ends on Nov. 19, 2026, they must request Nov. 20, 2026 as the STEM OPT Extension start date. The system will then automatically calculate their STEM OPT Extension end date as Nov. 19, 2028, which is 24 months from the STEM OPT Extension start date.
How to Request a STEM OPT Extension I-20 from OIS
Students can request a STEM OPT Extension I-20 from OIS through Trojan International. Students are required to pay a $200 administrative processing fee* to OIS before completing the rest of the form.

After receiving the STEM OPT Extension I-20 from OIS, students must file Form I-765 online via their myUSCIS account.

Important Deadline Considerations
Students may file Form I-765 and all supporting documents as early as 90 days before their Post-Completion OPT EAD end date and no later than their Post-Completion OPT EAD end date.
After receiving their STEM OPT I-20 from OIS, students must file Form I-765 and all supporting documents within 60 days of the I-20 issue date.
USCIS follows Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) for submission deadlines. Your application must be submitted by 23:59 UTC on the specified deadline, regardless of your local time zone. To avoid denials for missed filing deadlines, we strongly recommend submitting your application at least one day before the due date. Please plan accordingly and confirm UTC conversions for your time zone.
USCIS will deny any application received more than 60 days after the Form I-20 issue date or after the Post-Completion OPT EAD end date without exception. Students who are at risk of missing a deadline should contact OIS immediately.

Before You File
Make sure you are physically present in the United States when you file the Form I-765. Filing from outside the United States will result in a denial of your Form I-765.
Ensure your bank account has sufficient funds to cover the non-refundable Form I-765 filing fee to avoid USCIS rejecting your application.
Carefully review our guide to filing online Form I-765 for a STEM OPT Extension to avoid mistakes that could lead to a rejection, request for evidence, intent to deny or denial of your application.
How to File the Form I-765
Students will need to upload a copy of their hand-signed STEM OPT Extension I-20 — along with other supporting documents — and pay the non-refundable Form I-765 filing fee using a credit or debit card.
Students who want a response from USCIS before the estimated processing time can apply for Premium Processing for an additional fee.

Students who want a response from USCIS before the estimated processing time can apply for Premium Processing for an additional fee.
To apply for Premium Processing, students can either request it when initially filing the I-765 application or file Form I-907, Request for Premium Processing Service, at a later time. USCIS guarantees a response within 30 business days of filing for students who apply for Premium Processing.
Moving or Changing Your U.S. Address While Form I-765 Is Pending
If students anticipate moving while their Form I-765 is pending with USCIS, OIS recommends using a friend’s or family member’s mailing address for the I-765 application.
If students use their own address on their I-765, OIS does not recommend changing it until after the student has been approved and received the EAD. Doing so can cause delays and/or denial of Form I-765 due to mismatched addresses.
If students move from their mailing address, they must notify USCIS by completing the online USCIS Change of Address form to try to prevent USCIS from sending their EAD to the incorrect address.

Changes to Employment While Form I-765 Is Pending With USCIS
OIS strongly advises against changing employers while a STEM OPT Extension is pending with USCIS to avoid complications, delays or potential denials.
If the change of employer is unavoidable and a student needs to change employers while their STEM OPT Extension application is pending, they must follow these steps within 10 days of the change:
Step 1: End Employment With Your Previous Company (If Applicable)
If the employment ended before the STEM OPT Extension start date, submit the OPT Employment Update in Trojan International and complete steps 1, 2B and 3.
If the employment ended on or after the requested STEM OPT Extension start date, submit the STEM OPT Extension Final I-983 Self-Evaluation Report in Trojan International.
Step 2: Add Employment With Your New Company
Submit the STEM OPT Employment Update in Trojan International and complete steps 1, 2A and 3. There is a 10-business-day processing time from the date OIS receives your completed request.
Step 3: Submit Updated Information to USCIS

Step 3: Submit Updated Information to USCIS
OIS will email the updated STEM OPT Extension I-20 with the new employer information to the student’s USC email account. Print, sign and date the Form I-20 by hand and in black ink and make a copy.
Then, create a letter addressed to USCIS that includes your full name, I-797 receipt number, and your new employer’s E-Verify name and E-Verify number.
Finally, upload a copy of the hand-signed Form I-20 and the letter addressed to USCIS to the “Unsolicited Evidence” section of your I-765 application through your myUSCIS account.
Photo and Biometric Requirements
In December 2025, USCIS updated its policy on how photographs are collected and reused for immigration applications.
At this time, OPT and STEM OPT applicants must still submit two passport-style photos that meet U.S. Department of State passport photograph requirements, in accordance with current USCIS and OIS instructions.

Please regularly check your email, USPS mail and USCIS online account for a biometrics notice and to ensure your mailing address is up to date. If you receive any USCIS notice about photos or biometrics and have questions, submit the Request to Review USCIS Notice Form and then attend OIS advising for assistance.
If you have been notified that a biometrics appointment will be scheduled but have not received your biometrics appointment notice within two weeks, you should submit a USCIS Case Inquiry for Non-Delivery of Notice.

Social Media Vetting
USCIS has expanded the use of social media review in certain immigration applications. As a result, officers will conduct a closer review of a student’s immigration history and compliance with U.S. laws and students’ online activity may be considered as part of USCIS’s vetting process.
Promoting or supporting anti-American or antisemitic views will be considered serious negative factors and may lead to a denial of the application. The new policy is effective Aug. 19, 2025, and applies to both pending requests and those filed on or after that date.

STEM OPT Rejection, Request for Evidence, Notice of Intent to Deny or Denial
USCIS may send students an I-797C Notice of Action: Rejection, Request for Evidence (RFE), or an I-797C Notice of Action: Denial. If you receive one of these notices, you must submit the Request to Review USCIS Notice form to receive further guidance. After submitting the form, an advisor will review your case and follow up with the next steps.
Rejection
If an application is rejected, the student will receive an I-797C Notice of Action: Rejection. USCIS will indicate the reason for rejection on the I-797C. A student who receives a rejection notice should:
Submit the Request to Review USCIS Notice form.
Meet with an advisor during OIS drop-in advising to determine eligibility to resubmit Form I-765.
If eligible, request an updated STEM OPT I-20 using the STEM OPT I-20 Reprint Request in Trojan International.
File a new Form I-765, along with supporting documents, through myUSCIS no more than 60 days after the new STEM OPT I-20 issue date and before their Post-Completion OPT EAD end date.

Request for Evidence
A student may receive a Request for Evidence (RFE) if USCIS needs more information before processing their application. The RFE will specify which additional documents are required and the specific deadline for responding. The student will need to submit the Request to Review USCIS Notice form before responding to the RFE.
Notice of Intent to Deny
Upon review of the supporting evidence, USCIS may identify concerns and issue a Notice of Intent to Deny (NOID). This warning letter allows students to provide any new evidence addressing the concerns noted. The NOID includes a response deadline and failure to respond by that date can result in a denial of their application. The student will need to submit the Request to Review USCIS Notice form before responding to the NOID.

Denial
If an application is denied, the student will receive an I-797C Notice of Action: Denial for the STEM OPT application, which will indicate the reason for the denial. Due to USCIS processing times, a student denied may not be eligible to reapply if the end date of their Post-Completion OPT EAD has passed. A student who receives a denial notice should:
Submit the Request to Review USCIS Notice form.
Immediately meet with an advisor during OIS drop-in advising to determine eligibility to resubmit Form I-765.

File a new Form I-765, along with supporting documents, through myUSCIS no more than 60 days after the new STEM OPT I-20 issue date and before their Post-Completion OPT EAD end date.
Students who miss the filing deadline should join OIS drop-in advising to discuss their plans with an advisor.

General STEM OPT Requirements
In addition to complying with U.S. laws and immigration requirements, a student’s OPT must meet the following requirements. Failure to meet these requirements may result in the automatic termination of the student’s SEVIS record by SEVP and/or USCIS:
Employer must be enrolled in the Department of Homeland Security’s E-Verify system.
Employer must have a valid Employer Identification Number (EIN) issued by the Internal Revenue Service for tax purposes.
Employer must have and maintain a bona fide employer-employee relationship with the student
Employers must implement a formal training program to augment the students’ academic learning through practical experience.
Students must be paid for their practical training. Volunteer/unpaid training is not permitted on the STEM OPT Extension.

Employers must provide STEM OPT students with compensation comparable to that of U.S. workers performing similar duties and with similar educational and professional backgrounds. While OIS will verify that a student is receiving compensation, we cannot verify whether that compensation is appropriate for the position. This responsibility falls to the employer, who will attest in Section 4 of Form I-983 that the compensation is appropriate.
When applying for the STEM OPT Extension, students must begin working for the employer on or before the STEM OPT Extension start date.
The employment must be directly related to the student’s STEM-designated degree program.
Students must work 20 hours or more per week.
Students and their employers must attest to the information on the Form I-983.

Options for F-1 Students After STEM OPT Extension Ends
Once students reach the end of their STEM OPT Extension authorization period, they will have a 60-day grace period to remain in the United States and prepare for one of the following next steps.
New Program of Study at USC

chunks.title: STEM OPT Extension - USC OIS

New Program of Study at USC
Students must apply to their new program, be admitted and be issued a new I-20 from the USC Graduate Admission office before the end of the grace period. Proof of funding is required to issue the new I-20. Please contact the USC Graduate Admission office with questions regarding I-20 issuance; the request category should be “immigration matters.”
Transfer to Another Institution
Students must apply to another institution, be admitted and have their USC SEVIS record transferred out to the new institution before the end of the 60-day grace period. In addition, the start date at the transfer-in school must be within five months of the last date the student is on STEM OPT. For instructions on requesting a SEVIS transfer, refer to our page on attending another institution.
Depart the United States
Students may choose to depart the United States upon completion of their STEM OPT. They must depart by the end of their 60-day grace period.

Frequently Asked Questions
What is the $200 OIS STEM OPT Extension administration fee?
Students requesting a STEM OPT Extension I-20 from OIS will be required to pay a non-refundable $200 fee. This fee supports OIS services related to U.S. Department of Homeland Security reporting requirements and maintenance of status throughout the period of request and STEM OPT Extension employment.
Extended services provided to STEM OPT Extension students include I-20 travel endorsements, review and processing of mandated reports, and continued access to advisors for questions pertaining to their F-1 status and STEM OPT Extension employment matters.

What are the requirements for STEM OPT Extension eligibility based on a prior degree?
Refer to our page on getting a STEM OPT Extension based on a prior degree for more information.
What are common, avoidable reasons for STEM OPT Extension rejections or denials?
The following are common reasons for USCIS to reject a STEM OPT Extension:
If USCIS receives the Form I-765 STEM OPT Extension application after a student’s OPT EAD end date, the application will be denied.
USCIS denies any application received more than 60 days after the “issued date” on page 1 of the STEM OPT Extension I-20, even if an application is submitted before the OPT EAD end date.
If a student’s signature is missing or invalid on the Form I-20, USCIS will deny the application. Students must sign I-20s by hand in black ink; USCIS does not accept typed or electronic student signatures.
If a student’s application is returned or rejected for any reason, or if they receive a Request for Evidence (RFE) or denial notice, the student must contact OIS immediately before responding to USCIS.
What U.S. mailing address should students use on the Form I-765?

chunks.title: STEM OPT Extension - USC OIS
chunks.text:

What U.S. mailing address should students use on the Form I-765?
OIS recommends students use a U.S. mailing address they can reliably retrieve mail from for up to six months after filing their STEM OPT Extension application — this may require using a friend’s or relative’s address.
Students are strongly advised not to change their U.S. mailing address while their STEM OPT Extension application is pending with USCIS, as this can delay the processing and timely receipt of their EAD.
Refer to the guide to filing form I-765 above for more information. USPS does not forward mail from USCIS, even if a student has signed up for mail forwarding. If the EAD is undeliverable due to a change of address, it will be returned to USCIS. The student will not be notified if this happens.
How do students report a change of address to USCIS and OIS if they move while their STEM OPT Extension application is pending?
Students must notify USCIS by completing the online USCIS Change of Address form. They must also notify OIS by completing the SEVIS U.S. Address and Contact Update in Trojan International.

chunks.title: STEM OPT Extension - USC OIS
chunks.text:
ng the online USCIS Change of Address form. They must also notify OIS by completing the SEVIS U.S. Address and Contact Update in Trojan International.
Does USCIS accept students’ electronic signatures on I-20s?
No. Students must provide a wet signature (i.e., hand signed in black ink) on their Form I-20s. A student’s typed or electronic signature on a Form I-20 will not be accepted.
Can a student remain in the United States if their application is pending?
Yes. Students who have filed a timely STEM OPT application may remain in the United States while their OPT application is pending with USCIS.
Can students file a STEM OPT Extension application with USCIS while they are abroad?
No, students must be present in the United States at the time of submitting the STEM OPT Extension application. Otherwise, the STEM OPT Extension will be denied.
Can students with a pending STEM OPT Extension application continue working?
Students who file a timely application with USCIS may continue working after their Post-Completion OPT EAD expires until they receive the final decision from USCIS on the application (i.e., approved or denied) or for 180 days — whichever comes first.

Can students travel while their STEM OPT Extension is pending and after it is approved? If so, what documents do the students need?
Travel document requirements while a STEM OPT Extension is pending or approved are available on our reentry requirements page.
Can students cancel their STEM OPT Extension after it has been approved?
STEM OPT Extension cannot be canceled after it is approved, but students may choose to forfeit their STEM OPT Extension.
Students who wish to forfeit their STEM OPT Extension and return to their home country must notify OIS and submit a Form I-983 Final Self-Evaluation through Trojan International to complete their SEVIS record. Refer to the STEM OPT Extension reporting requirements for further guidance.

Failure to report departure information to OIS may result in the automatic termination of the student’s SEVIS record due to exceeding the allowable unemployment limit (90 days during standard OPT or 150 days total for students participating in a STEM OPT Extension). This could negatively impact future U.S. visa applications.
Can students enroll in classes while on STEM OPT Extension?
Per USCIS regulations, students may not be enrolled in a certificate or degree-seeking in-person or online program while on STEM OPT Extension. Students may take only classes that are avocational or recreational and incidental to their employment.
Can students work remotely on STEM OPT Extension?
Yes, students may work remotely in another state within the United States. They must report their remote address as their employer’s onsite address and continue to comply with all STEM OPT reporting requirements.
Can students work for more than one employer while on STEM OPT Extension?

chunks.title: STEM OPT Extension - USC OIS
chunks.text:
ite address and continue to comply with all STEM OPT reporting requirements.
Can students work for more than one employer while on STEM OPT Extension?
Yes; however, the student must file a Form I-983 for each employer. In addition, the student must work at least 20 hours per week, and each employer must meet all remaining eligibility requirements.
What do students who change from STEM OPT Extension to H1B need to report to OIS?
Students must submit their Form I-983, along with a completed final self-evaluation, via Trojan International. Refer to the STEM OPT Extension reporting requirements for further guidance.
What are students’ options after STEM OPT Extension ends?
Students are allowed to remain in the United States for up to 60 days after the approved STEM OPT Extension end date printed on their EAD. This period of time is called a “grace period.”
During this time, students may not work and may not leave and reenter the United States as F-1 students. During their 60-day grace period, students may:
Begin a new degree program at USC. Students must apply to the new program, be admitted and be issued a Change of Education Level Form I-20 from the USC Graduate Admission office.

Transfer their SEVIS record to another school. Students must submit a SEVIS Transfer Out Request to OIS.
Change their visa status. USCIS must receive and approve the application to change the immigration status before the end of the grace period.
Depart from the United States.
There’s a mistake on my EAD due to a USCIS Error. What should I do?
If your EAD contains an error due to a mistake made by USCIS, you will not be required to file a new Form I-765 or pay the application filing fee. To request a replacement EAD due to a USCIS error, follow these steps:
Request a reprint of your Form I-20 showing your STEM OPT Extension is approved by submitting an I-20 Reprint Request. This step is optional.
Make a photocopy of the incorrect EAD. You must keep a copy on file for your personal records.
Assemble the following documents:
The original card containing the error
A detailed letter of explanation of the card error
Copy of the most recently issued STEM OPT Extension I-20

Mail your request to the center that processed your STEM OPT Extension application and make sure you get a tracking number. Check the USCIS website for the most up-to-date addresses. USCIS will process your EAD replacement request within about 30 days.
If you are a student who applied for STEM OPT Extension via Premium Processing and received an incorrect EAD due to a USCIS error, please email psc-premium.processing@uscis.dhs.gov, explain the situation and attach a scanned copy of your EAD with the error for further guidance from USCIS.
My EAD got lost or stolen. What should I do?
If your EAD has been lost, stolen, or damaged, you will need to submit an application for a replacement EAD with USCIS by following these steps:
Request a reprint of your I-20 showing your STEM OPT Extension is approved by submitting an I-20 Reprint Request.

Your reason for applying should be “replacement of lost, stolen or damaged employment authorization document.”
Select “yes” for the question “Have you previously filed Form I-765?”

USCIS will process your EAD replacement request within about three months.
What time zone does USCIS use for the I-765 filing deadline?
USCIS follows Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) for submission deadlines. UTC is typically seven to eight hours ahead of Pacific Time, depending on whether Daylight Saving Time or Standard Time is in effect.
To avoid missing your filing deadline, we strongly recommend submitting your Form I-765 at least one day in advance of the due date.

What Is Post-Completion OPT?
Post-Completion OPT is a type of work authorization for students in F-1 status, allowing them to work in the United States for up to 12 months after completing their degree program. It is one of three types of Optional Practical Training (OPT) available to USC students.
Employment must be directly related to the student’s major field of study at USC. The student is required to maintain F-1 status and continue to report to OIS during the Post-Completion OPT period.
The OPT application will require a Form I-20 with the OPT recommendation on page 3 issued by OIS before filing a formal application using the Form I-765 to USCIS.
Back to Top
Eligibility Requirements for Post-Completion OPT
To be eligible for OPT, students:
Must have maintained F-1 status for a minimum of one academic year (i.e., two consecutive academic semesters, not including summer sessions).
Must have confirmed eligibility for graduation with their academic department/unit before initiating the OPT application process.

chunks.title: Post-Completion OPT - USC OIS

Must have confirmed eligibility for graduation with their academic department/unit before initiating the OPT application process.
Must not have accrued 12 months or more of full-time Curricular Practical Training (CPT) at their current degree level. Part-time CPT does not impact OPT eligibility.
Must not have previously completed OPT at the same degree level or a higher degree level. OPT can only be used once per degree level.
Must have submitted the OPT application to USCIS as early as 90 days before their program end date and no later than 60 days after their program end date. USCIS will not accept applications received 60 days or more beyond the program end date. In addition to these filing dates, there are other important deadlines a student must consider when applying for OPT, which will be addressed below.
Must be in the United States to file Form I-765.
Do not need a job or a job offer to apply.
Back to Top
How to Apply for Post-Completion OPT

Student submits OPT I-20 Request in Trojan International.
Student receives OPT I-20 from OIS via USC email.

A student can request the OPT I-20 from OIS as early as 90 days before their program end date, which is printed on the Form I-20. This date must align with the student’s actual degree conferral date. Students who are graduating early (before the end date on their I-20) must inform OIS by submitting a SEVIS Final Semester Check so that their program end date can be shortened before requesting an OPT I-20 from OIS.

Sometimes, there are delays in USCIS processing and USCIS is unable to adjudicate the Form I-765 by the recommended OPT start date. In these cases, USCIS will use the date it adjudicated the application as the new OPT start date and automatically calculate 12 months from that date as the OPT end date.
However, the OPT 14-month rule mandates that Post-Completion OPT be completed within 14 months of your program’s end date. Because the 12-month OPT period must fit within this 14 month window, any delays in processing can reduce your total working time to fewer than 12 months.
Due to unexpected delays that lead to changes in dates, students must wait for their EAD from USCIS to verify the actual start and end dates of approval.
